newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL-Japan key discount rate seen flat until 1998.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Japan key discount rate seen flat until 1998.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is likely to maintain Japan's official discount rate at its current record-low level at least until early next year, leading economists predicted in a Reuters poll released on Thursday.

Of 31 economists at research institutes, banks and brokerages who responded to questions on interest rates, all but one expected the BOJ to leave the official discount rate (ODR) unchanged at 0.5 percent at least until October.
Most also felt that the central bank would leave the key rate unchanged until sometime next year.
The official discount rate is the rate the central bank charges on loans to commercial banks.
Michael Hartnett, senior economist for Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, said the time will not be ripe for an interest rate increase until the April-June quarter of 1998.

"It (the BOJ) is waiting for three things to happen: One, (it is waiting for) bank lending to pick up; two, it is waiting for business conditions at small companies to pick up; and, three, it is waiting for consumer spending to pick up," Hartnett said.

"All three are unlikely to occur together before the second quarter of 1998," he added. At that time, Hartnett said, he felt the BOJ would raise the discount rate by 0.5 percentage point to one percent.

Richard Jerram, economist at ING Barings Securities, said the issue is not so much when BOJ is going to raise the ODR, but whether the discount rate is will keep rising or whether an increase will be just a one-off event.
"Most people think it's going to be lifted before the end of the fiscal year," he said, but added, "Even at one percent, it is still pretty low."

Susumu Kato, chief economist at BZW Securities in Japan and the only economist surveyed who predicted the BOJ would raise the discount rate before October, said the present interest rate level was too low in relation to economic conditions.
"Judging from current production activity and conditions in the labour market...an adjustment (rise) in interest rates can come at any time," Kato said.

Kato said he expected the BOJ to raise the discount rate by 0.5 percentage point, to one percent, in the July-September quarter, when it is likely to be able to confirm that the economy has recovered somewhat after a drop-off in April-June.
Kato said employment is increasing and salaries are rising, and this is likely to lead to a recovery in consumption.
"From the point of view of income, I think there is very little risk that the economy will falter from here," he said.
Keeping interest rates low in the face of such improving economic conditions will only hamper the recovery, Kato said.
"I think to maintain a situation in which returns from assets are practically zero percent will be detrimental to the economy," he said.
The survey was conducted from July 7 to July 9.
